subject.title: fix(agents): skip error classification for clean non-zero exits

question: What explicit contract should identify a non-zero exec result as expected and suppressible without hiding ordinary command failures?
rationale: The existing `completed` status only means that the process terminated normally, so source inspection cannot infer which non-zero codes the product should consider semantically successful.

options.title: Require explicit semantic success
options.body: Preserve non-zero failure classification unless the exec producer or invocation supplies an explicit accepted-result signal, then test both accepted and failing outcomes.

options.title: Suppress warnings only
options.body: Keep internal non-zero failure state but selectively suppress the final warning for an explicitly defined recoverable condition, accepting a narrower presentation-only policy.

options.title: Keep current behavior
options.body: Retain non-zero failure warnings and require commands that intentionally accept a code to encode that intent in the shell invocation.

recommendation.title: Require explicit semantic success
recommendation.body: Preserve non-zero failure classification unless the exec producer or invocation supplies an explicit accepted-result signal, then test both accepted and failing outcomes.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant exec outcome contract, agent-event handling, and warning policy are concentrated in this person's merged feature history.
